title: tk cloud trace: read a run's model conversation, tool calls and cache stats
description:
There is no way to see what a cloud run actually said or decided. tk factory has deploy/setup/status and tk cloud has run/stop/status; none of them reads a conversation, and D1 deliberately holds control-plane state only (runs, signals, dispatch_log, run_gateway_token, run_image, run_progress) — no messages.

The data already exists and is complete. AI Gateway keeps every proxied call, filterable by metadata.run_id, and serves full bodies from two detail endpoints: GET /ai-gateway/gateways/{gw}/logs/{id}/request returns the whole message array, and .../response returns choices, tool_calls and usage. Each log row also carries usage_metadata.input_cached_tokens, which is the only way to measure whether prefix caching is actually hitting — the l8z acceptance criterion. Proven by hand on run_62c289d1: 20 calls, 999,040 input tokens, 446,208 cached, and per-call rates swinging between 92 percent and 0 percent.

Two different things want two commands, so do not conflate them:
- tk cloud logs <run> — the harness stdout/stderr already streamed to R2, which is what the container printed.
- tk cloud trace <run> — the model conversation: message roles, tool calls and their arguments, tokens in/out and cached per call, cost per call.

Suggested flags for trace: --json for the raw rows, --call N to dump one exchange in full, --tools for just the tool calls, --cache for the per-call cache table that answers the caching question at a glance.

Note the constraint: D21 fixes the operator-to-orchestrator COMMAND vocabulary at run/stop/status/answer. These are read-only observation commands and do not steer a run, so they do not widen that vocabulary — but say so explicitly in the design doc when this lands, or the next reader will think D21 was violated.
